newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistani opposition calls strike for Sunday.
newsitem.headline: Pakistani opposition calls strike for Sunday.

text.p: A Pakistani opposition alliance has called for a general strike on Sunday to protest the killing of an activist from the ethnic Mohajir National Movement (MQM), a party spokesman said on Saturday.

"We have asked the people to keep their businesses and offices shut on Sunday (to protest) against the extra-judicial killing of our party member, Mohammad Farooq, by the authorities on Thursday," MQM spokesman Shoaib Bukhari told Reuters.
The call for the general strike was given by the Action Committee of the nine-party alliance, which met at the MQM headquarters in Karachi on Friday.
Police said Farooq was killed in an encounter in Karachi's central Gulbhar area.

"The terrorists had attacked a police party, which returned the fire. One of the terrorists was wounded in the shoot-out who later died in the hospital, while others managed to flee," a senior police official said.
The government blames the MQM for most of the violence in Karachi, where more than 2,000 people were killed in 1995. So far this year 350 people have been killed.

The MQM represents Urdu-speaking people who migrated from India at the time of the partition in 1947 and their decendants. It has called more than half a dozen strikes in Sindh province this year to protest the killing of its workers by police.
